subject: Happy Hour invitation, Humanoid Summit - Tokyo
text:
Dear [NAME],

Hope you're well. Saw you're coming to the Humanoid Summit next week and
wanted to extend an invite:

We're hosting a small happy hour the night before the summit kicks off
(Wednesday May 27, 6-9pm) at Bar Cocktail Works in Shinagawa, 5 min walk
from the conference venue. ~30 founders, execs, and engineering leads
working across humanoid robotics and broader physical AI. Drinks, bites, no
panels, no pitches.

Boston Dynamics, Woven by Toyota, Dyna Robotics, and others.

We would love to have you attend. Let me know if you're available and I'll
send over the details.

subject: Just Called, Left VM - Spectacles Data Pipeline
text:
Hi [NAME],

I tried to call you earlier and left a message.

I noticed that the Spectacles team is hiring for an MLE, CV with a focus on
scene understanding, SLAM, and on-device optimization. That made me think
that the data pipeline, especially for complex sensor data, is scaling
faster than the data infrastructure can keep up.

We helped Woven by Toyota solve exactly that. Tighter feedback loops
between ground truth and model training at scale. I think it maps well to
what the Spectacles team is building.

Even if your internal tool is efficient for your team, I'd love to hear
more about data flywheel and model eval process in AR.

Do you have 20 mins to chat this week?

P.S. - Go Tritons! Class of '25

subject: Data infrastructure after speaking to some of the team
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been speaking to some of the [COMPANY] team, including Aethon, so
thought it would be worth reaching out to you. At Encord, we're the data
layer behind some of the largest physical AI companies globally: Skydio,
Woven by Toyota, and Boston Dynamics.

Across your ALDA STC portfolio, the recurring bottleneck we see is the
same: petabytes of multimodal sensor data, fragmented annotation pipelines,
and no clean line from collection to deployed-model feedback. Encord
consolidates that into one backbone so each business unit moves faster on
the same foundation.

Worth a 20 minute call? Even if there's no immediate fit, I can share what
we're seeing across similar defense-adjacent AI groups in APAC.

subject: Follow-on from [COMPANY] discussions
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been speaking to some members of the [COMPANY] team, and thought
it would be worth sending you this email.

At Encord, R&D groups like Honda Research Institute and Toyota's Woven
Planet use us to compress the data-side of the research loop: curating
multimodal datasets, annotating perception data, and iterating model evals
without standing up bespoke pipelines per project.

For [COMPANY]'s R&D portfolio (drone swarms, autonomy, defense AI),
the time we typically save is on the unglamorous middle: getting raw flight
and sensor data into a state where it's ready to train and re-train on.
Researchers spend more time on the model, less on the data plumbing.

Happy to walk through how it's set up at peer R&D groups. Worth 20 mins?

subject: The data-layer question behind VLAs and world models
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been speaking to some members of the [COMPANY] team, so thought
it would be worth speaking to you too.

At Encord, we sit underneath the physical-AI stack as the data layer
(collection, curation, multimodal annotation, eval) for teams training VLA
models, world models, and embodied agents.

If you're scanning frontier bets for [COMPANY]'s 3-5 year roadmap, the
question worth pressure-testing is: how will ST capture, curate, and align
the petabyte-scale multimodal streams that VLA and world-model training
will demand? Most groups discover the data layer is the rate-limiter on
capability, not the model side.

Happy to share what we're seeing across frontier-research groups (Toyota
Research, Forterra, and others) without a pitch.

subject: Follow-on from internal discussions
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been speaking to a few people at [COMPANY], hence thought it best
to email you as you may be the right person to speak to about this.

At Encord, we work with Physical AI teams on their ML data pipelines.

If you're the MLE shipping models on ST's drone or autonomy stack, your day
probably involves more sensor-data wrangling, label QA, and eval debugging
than you'd like. Encord is where teams at Pickle Robot, Dexterity, and
Woven shifted that work off the MLE's plate: native multimodal (video +
LiDAR + sensor) annotation, programmatic curation by embeddings and active
learning, model-output evaluation against ground truth, and a Python SDK +
webhooks so it slots into your existing training stack.

If labeling throughput, dataset versioning, or eval iteration is your
friction point right now, worth a 20-min look.

subject: [COMPANY] conversation with the team
text:
